Folks — forwarding Nimbus' procurement request. They want concrete contract language for the CU and the SLA credit formula. Can we agree on a defensible definition that maps to our capacity management and also provides Nimbus the transparency they need?

Notes:
- They want to avoid benchmark-only definitions that don't reflect mixed workloads.
- Procurement timeline: close by first week of July.

Proposed starting point (draft for redline):
1) Definition: "Reserved Capacity Unit (RCU)" means one GPU-hour of capacity on Redwood's Dedicated pool, equivalent to one A100-80GB GPU-hour running Redwood's reference inference runtime with a 2048-token context and baseline request profile.
2) Measurement Profile: Throughput guarantees measured as the 95th percentile (p95) tokens/sec across requests for the canonical profile in a calendar minute; we will publish a test harness and reference dataset to validate.
3) Service Credits: For each month, if observed p95 throughput for the committed pool falls below the guaranteed p95 for more than X contiguous minutes, credits are applied as a percentage of that month's committed fee according to the attached table (see draft). Credits capped at 100% of monthly committed fee per month.

Marissa — can you create a short CSV example of how we translate RCUs to expected concurrent requests for chat vs long-gen? Karthik — any commercial flexibility to accommodate a 'workload-weighted CU' that lets Nimbus commit to an annual CU pool but have credits tuned to actual mix? Neha — need redline language that avoids open-ended audit/metric disputes.

Thanks,
Priyom

Thanks for the draft. I've prepared redline language and a short rationale — pasted below for quick review. I recommend we include 3 attachments: (1) a one-page CU definition, (2) a sample credit schedule, (3) a CSV with throughput mappings. I'm attaching the drafts to this thread.

Redline excerpt (legal-friendly):
"Reserved Capacity Unit (RCU). For purposes of this Agreement, a 'Reserved Capacity Unit' (RCU) is defined as one hour of reserved inference capacity on Redwood's Dedicated pool, measured on Redwood-managed hardware equivalent to an NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU. The RCU baseline is established using Redwood's reference inference runtime executing a canonical test profile (2048 token context length, sequence composition as published) and expressed as an expected p95 throughput value in tokens-per-second. If Redwood changes the reference hardware class, Redwood will provide 90 days' notice and a migration plan preserving economic equivalence.

Measurement and Validation. Throughput guarantees are measured as the 95th percentile (p95) tokens-per-second using Redwood's telemetry and trace data, aggregated per calendar minute. Nimbus may request one validation test per quarter using the published test harness and will be provided exported logs for the validation window. Disputes will be escalated to a joint technical review within 10 business days.

Service Credits. If the observed p95 throughput for the committed pool remains below the guaranteed p95 for a contiguous period exceeding thirty (30) minutes in a calendar month, Nimbus shall be entitled to a service credit as set forth in the schedule attached hereto. Credits shall be computed as a percentage of the impacted month's committed fee, prorated to the duration below target, and capped at the lesser of 100% of the monthly committed fee or the total monthly fees attributable to the impacted RCUs.

I kept the audit/validation process explicit to limit ongoing disputes and provided notice/migration language to protect both sides. If you OK this wording I'll add the attachments and produce a PDF redline.

Neha
General Counsel (Acting), Redwood Inference
